record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: What is the physical interpretation of the modular parameter tau_B, obtained from the Belyi pair, in the superconformal field theory described by a brane tiling?

evidence.quote: Question 24. What is the physical interpretation of τB in the brane tiling’s SCFT?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A brane tiling is a bipartite graph drawn on a two-dimensional torus that encodes the data of a four-dimensional N=1 superconformal gauge theory arising on a stack of D3-branes probing a toric Calabi–Yau threefold singularity: faces correspond to gauge groups, edges to bifundamental chiral multiplets, and vertices (black/white) to superpotential terms (with signs given by vertex color). To any brane tiling one can associate a Belyi pair (E_B, β), where E_B is an elliptic curve (a complex torus) and β: E_B → P^1 is a holomorphic map ramified only over {0, 1, ∞}; the bipartite graph is recovered as the preimage β^{-1}([0,1]) with black/white vertices over 0 and 1 and faces over ∞, and the ramification profiles match the valences of the tiling. The complex structure of E_B is specified by a modular parameter τ_B ∈ H/SL(2,Z) (the upper half-plane modulo the modular group), referred to as the Belyi modular parameter of the tiling.

Independently, the superconformal R-charges of the gauge theory (determined by a-maximization) endow the tiling torus with an isoradial embedding, hence with its own complex structure parameter τ_R ∈ H/SL(2,Z) (the "R-charge" or "isoradial" complex structure).

Problem. Give a physical interpretation, intrinsic to the four-dimensional superconformal field theory associated with the brane tiling, of the Belyi modular parameter τ_B. Specifically, identify a physical observable, coupling, or geometric/dynamical quantity of the SCFT (or of its gravity/string-theoretic dual) whose value is determined by τ_B, and explain in what sense τ_B encodes that quantity, distinguishing it from the isoradial parameter τ_R derived from the R-charges.
artifact.status_search_result: The relationship between the Belyi complex structure τ_B of a brane tiling and the isoradial/R-charge complex structure τ_R has been studied (notably in works on toric CFTs, permutation triples, and the "beta ansatz"), but a clean, intrinsic physical interpretation of τ_B in the SCFT itself does not appear to have been established. No source located identifies a definitive physical meaning of τ_B; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Toric CFTs, permutation triples, and Belyi pairs
status_evidence.snippet: Brane tilings are encoded in permutation triples that correspond to Belyi pairs (E_B, β), endowing the tiling torus with a complex structure τ_B.
status_evidence.claim: The Belyi pair gives rise to a complex structure τ_B on the brane tiling torus.

status_evidence.title: The beta ansatz: a tale of two complex structures
status_evidence.snippet: Compares the Belyi complex structure with the complex structure obtained from the R-charges via isoradial embedding, raising the question of their physical relation.
status_evidence.claim: There are two distinct complex structures (Belyi and R-charge) on the tiling torus, and the physical meaning of τ_B is not pinned down.
